focus: Mechanism D - enforcement carried by templates and validate.sh
noveltyJustification: The ANCHORS_VALID required-anchor lever and its corpus-wide regrade cost are new; that both paths run validate.sh was known from iteration 1.
keyQuestions: For each candidate mechanism (AGENTS.md gate, shared step reference, hook injection, template and validate.sh enforcement, advisor-driven command invocation), what does it cost and what does it break?
ruledOut: A new validator rule for plan decisions
Adding a required plan anchor at the current template version
Relying on the validator for ordering

graphEvents.label: Can templates and the validator carry the check
Both paths run the same validate.sh
A rule is a script plus a registry row
A new anchor regrades every existing plan

findings.label: validate.sh is the one check both paths run so a rule needs no cross-runtime delivery story
A rule is a shell script plus a registry row, which is the expensive part
A rule can read HTML comments so a comment-borne convention is detectable
ANCHORS_VALID already makes every template anchor mandatory for v2.3+ documents
A new required anchor regrades every existing v2.4 plan document
Level scaling is native to the validator so a Level 1 exemption is a condition not a gate
The validator sees artifacts never sequence so it cannot hold the workflow process checks
Per-turn token cost is zero because the validator is executed not read
The repair loop is bounded and already ends in a written open question in goal.md
